newsitem.title: NEPAL: British climber injured on Nepal peak rescued.
newsitem.headline: British climber injured on Nepal peak rescued.

text.p: A Briton seriously injured in a fall on Mount Kanchenjunga, the world's third tallest peak, was rescued by helicopter on Monday, rescuers said.
They said Rodney McArthur was picked up from 5,180 metres (17,000 feet) on the 8,586-metre (28,169 ft) mountain in eastern Nepal.
"He is really serious," Colonel Gunjaman Lama, the pilot of the army helicopter that brought the climber to the Nepali capital, told Reuters.
Lama said McArthur sustained rib and head injuries when he fell while climbing on Sunday. The 34-year-old major in the British army was taken to hospital from the airport.
McArthur, from Londonderry, Northern Ireland, was climbing Kanchenjunga with 12 Americans and two other Britons.
Further details of the accident were not immediately available.
Lama said Kanchenjunga was covered by thick clouds and lashed by strong winds and heavy rain following cyclonic storms over the Bay of Bengal.
A Korean expedition, a Slovak group and a Spanish team are still on Kanchenjunga, located on the far eastern tip of Nepal bordering India.
Two people died and three went missing last week on the Tibetan side of the world's highest peak, Mount Everest. The Nepal Himalayas contain eight of the world's 14 highest peaks.
